what: proc-macro-srv ProcMacroSrv::expand (src/lib.rs) spawns and joins a thread with an 8 MiB stack per expansion, about 20 us per miss (mmap, guard mprotect, clone, futex join, munmap, first-touch faults), so a macro thread locals end with each expansion. rustc expands a crate macros on one thread, so thread locals live across a crate expansions there. Decide whether one expander thread per connection and calling crate (the client sends the calling crate, which Kept::expand_in already has) is the semantics to keep: it costs nothing per call and is closer to rustc, but changes what a stateful macro sees against today. The doc docs/v2/plan/lanes/usercode/speed-of-light-macros.md counts it; macros.md already says request: a pool.
